FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: onion confit
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} sliced and melted two hours under a lid, then uncovered and left to caramelise with {1_plur} and red {2_plur} until they turn almost black and syrupy.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: onion tatin
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} halved and set cut side down in a {1_adj} caramel with vinegar, covered over with pastry and turned out after baking. The principle of the apple tart, applied to the savoury.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cipolline in agrodolce
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: small whole {0_coll} glazed in balsamic vinegar and {1_plur}, with bay. Eaten cold, and they keep a week, gaining by the day.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bacon and onion jam
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {2_coll} rendered slowly, {0_coll} stewed down in its fat with brown {1_plur} and cider vinegar. Spread on a burger or on toast, indifferently.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: green tomato jam
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} that never ripened before the frosts, sliced and steeped overnight in {1_plur}, then cooked with {2_plur} until they turn translucent. Nothing is wasted in the garden.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: ketchup
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} reduced for hours with {2_plur}, vinegar, {1_coll} and a bag of whole spices lifted out at the end. The word comes from a Chinese fish brine, and there was no tomato in it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tomato and date chutney
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {2_coll} stewed in palm {1_plur} with the five Bengali spices, until it coats the spoon. Served at the end of the meal, before the sweet, to clean the mouth.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tomato tatin
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} candied in a {1_adj} and {2_adj} caramel, packed side by side under a sheet of pastry and turned out warm. The sugar does not make them sweet: it concentrates them.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: beef teriyaki
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} sliced thin and seared, then lacquered with a reduction of {2_adj}, mirin and {1_adj} brushed on three times over. The shine is the object, not the sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: orange beef
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: strips of {0_adj} coated in starch and fried crisp, tossed in a {1_adj} syrup with vinegar and dried {2_adj} peel. The crust has to hold up under the sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: carbonnade with brown sugar
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised in brown {2_plur}, softened with brown {1_plur} and a slice of mustarded gingerbread that dissolves and binds the sauce. The bitterness of the beer and the sugar hold each other in balance.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: beef with prunes
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised with dried {2_coll} that fall apart at the end of the cooking and sweeten the juices by themselves. {1_coll} goes in only at the very last, and very little of it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: brown sugar brisket
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a {0_adj} brisket rubbed with brown {1_plur}, {2_plur} and smoked paprika, then smoked twelve hours. The sugar forms the black crust they call the bark, and it is the best of it.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: carottes Vichy
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} in rounds cooked uncovered in just enough water, {1_plur} and {2_plur}, until the liquid goes and leaves a shining glaze behind.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rotkohl
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: red {0_coll} shredded and braised an hour with grated {2_coll}, vinegar and {1_coll}, plus a single clove. The acid holds the colour; without it the cabbage turns blue.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sweet-and-sour beetroot
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked in their skins then marinated in a {1_adj} vinegar with mustard seed and dill. They take a week to come into balance and keep for months.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: daigaku imo
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: pieces of sweet potato fried and then coated in a {1_adj} caramel with soy, sown with black {2_plur}. University potato: the students of Tokyo bought them for next to nothing.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: zucca in agrodolce
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: slices of {0_adj} fried and then marinated hot in a {1_adj} vinegar with mint and garlic. Eaten cold the next day; on the day itself it is too violent.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: takuan
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a daikon dried in the sun for weeks until it will bend, then buried in rice bran with {1_plur} and salt. Bright yellow, crisp, and loud to chew.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sweet cucumber pickles
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {2_coll} finely sliced, drawn out in coarse salt then scalded in a {1_adj} vinegar with turmeric and mustard seed.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: sweet-and-sour pork
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} coated in starch and fried twice, thrown at the last moment into a {1_adj} sauce with vinegar and {2_coll}. Mixed too early, the coating collapses.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: vegetable achards
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cut into fine julienne, blanched then drowned in an oil with turmeric, ginger and vinegar, with just enough {1_adj} to round off the acid. They improve over three days.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: honey-glazed ham
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a joint of {0_adj} scored in a lattice and stuck with cloves, brushed with {1_plur} and {2_plur} every twenty minutes until an amber crust forms.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: honey and garlic chicken
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} seared then stewed in {1_coll}, crushed {2_coll} and a splash of vinegar, until the sauce reduces and clings to the flesh.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: miso and honey glazed salmon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated overnight in a paste of fermented {1_adj} and {2_adj}, then run under the grill. The sugar of the miso burns fast: you watch it without leaving the salamander.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tfaya tagine
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {2_coll} stewed with saffron, covered with a tfaya — {0_coll} stewed down for hours with dried {1_plur}, cinnamon and honey, until dark brown.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: mrouzia
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} confited with ras el hanout and smen, drowned in {1_plur} and loaded with fried {2_adj}. The honey and the salt kept the meat for weeks after the feast of the sacrifice.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: khoresh-e beh
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised with quinces in quarters, whose hard flesh melts within the hour and scents everything, sharpened with verjuice and sweetened with a little honey.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pork with cider and apples
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a roast of {0_adj} braised in {2_plur} with {1_coll} in quarters, half of which fall to a compote while the other half hold their shape. The juices reduce to a syrup on their own.
